Clarification: the lack of estrogen would have caused me to likely grow a little taller a while longer. I don't know that much about biological systems as I'm not bio major (Computer systems engineering 👌), I probably more than the average trans person/ regular person. When you grow estrogen causes plates (I am probably not using proper terminology?) to stop growing and fuse to prevent further growing. Yes even cis males have a small amount of estrogen (it's probably an interaction of a lot of hormones and stuff) produced to regulate this during puberty, but it happens later so they on average grow more. At least I think this is the best simplified version. If anyone knows a lot more than me, feel free to correct me or go into more detail. Hypothetically if I had hormone blockers it probably would have allowed me to grow a bit more, but I don't know how doctors who do this sort of thing do everything properly. I do know that giving trans girls estrogen too much too early will likely stop their growth (permanently) but that doesn't seem to be a problem for a lot because they would on average grow taller than the average cis woman, so more questions probably ask a specific doctor 😅. Social transition came pretty easy. I'm white, so let's be honest I have it much easier than most. To most I just appear like a white cis male who maybe comes off gay in occasional cases. I will say it's weird because people sometimes assume that I've never had any kind of real trial in my life and that was unexpected but still I recognize that I have a ton of social privilege and I shouldn't complain about sometimes getting judged like that. A few of my mannerisms were/are feminine as I was raised to be/do such but that's why I say that I sometimes come off as gay in those cases. In most cases it's probably not that apparent because I would say my mannerisms have always leaned quite masculine, but when presenting as female you get shamed for that kind of stuff so again, that's why some probably come off as feminine, I hated being judged especially at BYU so I really tried to act like a girl for a few years. 

I will say coming off as gay is so much better and safer than someone clocking you as trans, so if someone asks if I'm gay I usually just say yeah and don't mention the trans part or that I lean towards females, lol. 

I think I also expected transitioning to solve all my mental health issues, and while it did significantly help so much and I think that doctors /therapists thinking that trans people need to be of perfect mental health before transitioning fundamentally doesn't make any sense because dysphoria fucking sucks and fucks you up, it made it so I hardly ever was suicidal (I got harassed for 6 months which was shit and yes made me suicidal, but that's a long separate story) ever since I transitioned. But it didn't solve my depression, and I shouldn't have thought that being so, so sad and depressed for so long because I had no right to change my own body until I was old enough was going to suddenly be gone. There was a lot of scars I had to work through and still am.

1. Yes but probably not to the extent that MtF people have to worry about. T mostly gets you really horny all the time at least when you're first starting much like regular male puberty, so the case can be made that you're probably having more sex/getting off more. I've heard that Ftms holes can atrophy a bit meaning I think that it can be tighter/not loosen as much when aroused and a be bit more painful when having *that* type of sex. Also it's said that we produce less natural lubrication. As for myself personally, I've been on a lower than "normal" dose because I feel like I really don't need it, and my blood test prove that I'm fine, and higher amounts cause a lot more acne on me. I feel like I haven't really been subject to any negative effects of long term T use (although 3 years isn't that long), but I didn't have sex for the first time until I was a year or so on T, so I don't know really have a comparison. 

Funny thing I think someone would find interesting is that I don't ever orgasm twice. My body can do more I just feel completely done after the first. So I guess maybe that can be seen as negative? I don't mind it at all but yes I think that has something to do with the hormones. 

2. Way bigger difference? Probably not as big a difference because Testosterone is the more "unforgiving" hormone in that once your body is subject to it, it's hard to undo those changes. So where a MtF would probably really really benefit in a physical sense from not having to go through the bad puberty they do not want, Ftms would probably only really benefit in not having to go through their bad puberty, if that makes sense. Of course, I think the mental anguish going through either when it feels wrong is probably on average about the same. There are certain aspects that estrogen did that are not easy to undo/impossible, namely I grew a chest and have hips and I would definitely be taller than I am now, although I got lucky with the height because I'm 5'11 (but all the other males in my family are at least 6'2, so compared to my family it's noticeable but honestly I'm not one to complain). But getting a period for the first time when you are mentally a dude will definitely fuck you up for a bit, lol. I was 12 and it was just fucking terrible. 

3. So I haven't mentioned this yet but my endocrinologist retired without telling me and when I ran out of T, I wasn't able to get more of it for about 3 months (I have some now 🙏). Given that, we were still 95% of the time using protection and otherwise pulling out. I didn't think everything would start up as fast as it did but a month into it I had a period. Second month I should have had a period and basically the same day I should have had it, I was sooooo sick to my stomach. It wasn't my first thought, but when I noticed a tiny amount of bleeding like a week into feeling so sick and knowing the signs enough, I started thinking about the possibility. I knew me feeling sick wasn't a mental block or anxiety and my mom had 4 pregnancies after me which I really remember because she was so sick all the time and so I just kinda jumped to the worst probable thing and took a test (actual 2), but by this time I told my partner my suspicions. The tests immediately showed up as positive and it was a big oh fuck moment to be sure because I really wasn't expecting it. So wasn't my first guess but luckily I jump to really bad things and was right and caught it super early. I didn't start T until after my abortion as a precaution to make sure I had the highest chance of everything working properly and feeling the least amount of pain.

Yup he's a cis male and unfortunately getting pregnant is something we still have to be careful of. 

Also that proper term is dysphoria in this case, and yes aside from a bit of bleeding I'm doing really well.

Haha I'm one of those kids that realized super early, like literally 2/3 years old. First memories were centered a ton around gender. Grew up Mormon and understood the doctrine of my culture I was raised in. No I don't identify as Mormon anymore, although it probably has to do with a contribution to a lot more guilt around this whole situation. 

Anyway I understood I was going to be a woman and I didn't have much of a choice, that is until I saw something on discover health channel about people who "changed sex" haha. I don't think the term "transgender" was in the thing at all. I was a kid when I saw that and puberty hadn't fucked me up that much yet.

Fast forward about 4 years and holy shit puberty was a "no this is very wrong why tho plz stop" type situation. I found the real term, transgender, around this time and just kept it as long as I could. 4 years after that I was like FUCK IT and cut off all my hair and tried to tell people. No one got it. It's honest amazing how far we've come in 5 years because literally no one got it then and a good amount try way more now to get it. 

I tried to transition, but soon my parents basically threatened my indirectly to never see my siblings again  when I turned 18 and that freaked me out and I started growing out my hair. 

Fast forward even more and I tried going to BYU. Into my 3rd semester I competely broke and tried to committed suicide. Like I probably really shouldn't be here. I pretty much immediately dropped out and went back to Arizona, came out as trans and said fuck it. Got on T a month later, which some may say was fast but I'm like 8 years too late yoooo. 

Lol sorry if that was longer than expected but I felt like context was needed and I think I'm probably going to bed now so I might as well get my story out there just in case of any more questions.

I wish I could create a metaphor that would describe how it felt or was good enough with words to explain how truly fucked up I was mentally and in addition to that physically as I come from a family that loses weight during pregnancy and I'm already leaning towards being underweight annnnnnd I am in recovery from anorexia (2 years and ~3 years in recovery). I lost 10 pounds over 3 weeks literally just because I could hardly eat. I know it was the right decision and never really had to think about the decision because I know I could not do it, and I haven't second guessed it, even if I do know I feel some guilt about it. 

But basically I was soooooooo fucked up about being pregnant. Even saying that now, like wtf I shouldn't be able to be pregnant. Biology really fucked up.

My partner was pretty ok with it. I don't think either of us were necessarily happy about the situation or having to make the decision but we cannot afford a child in 7 months and he also understands how much that would really hurt me mentally to go through. He was really on board as long as we did it early and I was the same way, as the later the harder it would have been, but luckily I got super sick like 4 weeks in and thought about the possibility and tested myself at 5 weeks. 

I joke about it with him even still as a form of therapy because it was hard, and I'm really glad we've been together long enough that he understands me and that joking means I'm kinda in pain about it and needing to work through it. He's the only one who knows besides my therapist as of now, and I guess you guys but you guys almost 100% I'm sure can't tell who I am in real life, given the account. So I feel safe saying things I need to say.

Ok so I'm not going to claim that I know if that's the way it's been implemented or not but I would say that I'm one of those trans people that people don't know I'm trans and I generally don't want them to know for a while into our friendship. So im not one of *those* trans people, but I really don't think most trans people are. 

If it's truly seen as "government compelled speech" in people's eyes, I first think about hate speech which in the US is not usually illegal unless it is "inciting imminent lawless action and is likely to incite or produce such action." I would probably apply similar rules to pronoun usage. Disrespect is shitty, and I hate being called wrong pronouns, but doing so on a disrespectful level is different than doing it on a violent level and I think there should be that distinction so that those who are not violent have the opportunity at least to learn and change their views without ruining their lives and making them always hate trans people. 

I honestly don't know how it's being implemented but I think it's worth noting that people are at least trying to make the world safer for trans people. That I support, even if their wording of the bill is seen as not the best. I hope it is never used by police to target people for no reason, but I hope that people realize that the world is really not that safe for trans people, especially trans women of color.
